sights.address: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
sights.w: Golden Gate Park's fine-arts museum for American art, textiles and global cultures, wrapped in a copper Herzog & de Meuron building with a free 9th-floor observation tower over the park. Open Tue-Sun; one ticket also admits the Legion of Honor same day.

A neoclassical palace on the Lincoln Park cliffs (a Beaux-Arts copy of Paris's Legion of Honor) holding European painting and Rodin bronzes, with Lands End and Golden Gate views out front. Open Tue-Sun; admission covers same-day de Young entry.

sights.address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
sights.w: A natural-history museum, aquarium, planetarium and four-story indoor rainforest under one living roof in Golden Gate Park. A top family stop; open daily with Sunday opening at 11am.

sights.address: 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
sights.w: The oldest public Japanese garden in the US (1894), with a drum bridge, pagoda, koi ponds and a tea house; the birthplace of the American fortune cookie. Free entry Mon/Wed/Fri 9-10am.

sights.address: 100 John F Kennedy Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
sights.w: A gleaming white Victorian glasshouse (1879), the oldest wood-and-glass conservatory in North America, packed with tropical and aquatic plants. Open Thu-Tue; closed Wednesdays for maintenance.
55 acres and roughly 8,000 kinds of plants in Golden Gate Park, from a cloud-forest collection to a magnolia grove that's one of the best outside China. Open daily.
sights.k: Free for SF residents with ID; paid for non-residents.

sights.n: Dutch Windmill & Queen Wilhelmina Tulip Garden
sights.address: 1690 John F Kennedy Dr, San Francisco, CA 94121
sights.w: A 1903 Dutch-style windmill at Golden Gate Park's ocean edge, fronted by the Queen Wilhelmina tulip garden that blooms brightest in late winter and early spring. Free, open grounds.

sights.address: 680 Point Lobos Ave, San Francisco, CA 94121
sights.w: A rugged NPS coastal trail past cypress groves, shipwreck-strewn surf and the concrete ruins of the 1896 Sutro Baths, with the Golden Gate Bridge framed the whole way. Free; open daily.
sights.k: The adjacent Cliff House (1090 Point Lobos Ave) has been closed since 2020; a reopening has been announced for late 2026 but repeatedly delayed.

sights.address: 16th Ave & Moraga St, San Francisco, CA 94122
sights.w: A 163-step mosaic staircase in Golden Gate Heights, tiled in a sea-to-stars swirl by artists Aileen Barr and Colette Crutcher with the neighborhood; climb it to Grand View Park for a Sunset-and-ocean panorama. Free, always open.

The West Coast's flagship modern-art museum, expanded by Snohetta into seven gallery floors with a free ground-floor Richard Serra and a living wall on the sculpture terrace. Open daily except Wednesday.
One of the largest Asian art collections in the West, 18,000+ works spanning 6,000 years, housed in the old Beaux-Arts main library on Civic Center. Open Thu-Mon; closed Tue/Wed.
Daniel Libeskind's tilted blue-steel cube grafted onto a 1907 power substation, one of downtown's boldest buildings.
sights.k: CLOSED as an operating museum since December 2024 amid a financial crisis; in March 2026 the museum announced it is selling the Libeskind building, though it continues hosting some events through January 2027. The exterior remains a landmark to view.

sights.address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94111
sights.w: A pioneering hands-on science and perception museum sprawling across an Embarcadero pier, with 600+ tinker-with-it exhibits and adults-only After Dark Thursday nights. Open Tue-Sun.
A cluttered shrine to the Beat Generation across from City Lights, with Kerouac and Ginsberg letters, first editions and the car from the film of On the Road.
sights.k: Temporarily closed from December 2025 for a seismic (soft-story) retrofit, with reopening announced for mid-to-late 2026 - confirm before visiting.

sights.w: The twin-spired "Italian Cathedral of the West" on Washington Square, where Joe DiMaggio and Marilyn Monroe took wedding photos on the steps. Open daily.
In a former Presidio barracks, the story of Walt Disney himself - early drawings, the multiplane camera, Oscars and a huge model of Disneyland. Open Thu-Mon.
A monumental Beaux-Arts rotunda and colonnade left from the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition, mirrored in a swan lagoon in the Marina. Grounds are free and open daily.
A mile of Presidio sand with a full-frontal view of the Golden Gate Bridge; the north end is clothing-optional and the surf is strong (no swimming). Free, open daily.

A 14-acre park (opened 2022) built over the Presidio Parkway tunnels, linking Crissy Field to the Main Post with Golden Gate views, a nature-play Outpost for kids and picnic meadows. Free, open daily.
A French Gothic Episcopal cathedral atop Nob Hill with gilded Ghiberti "Gates of Paradise" doors and two labyrinths you can walk. Open daily; admission for general visiting.

sights.address: Peace Plaza, Post St & Buchanan St, San Francisco, CA 94115
sights.w: A five-tiered concrete stupa gifted by sister-city Osaka in 1968, the centerpiece of the Peace Plaza in one of only three remaining Japantowns in the US. Free, open plaza.
Mission San Francisco de Asis (1776), the city's oldest surviving building, with the original adobe chapel beside an ornate 1918 basilica and a historic cemetery. Open daily 9am-4pm.

sights.address: Dolores St & 19th St, San Francisco, CA 94114
sights.w: The Mission's sun-trap hillside lawn, part civic living room and part downtown-skyline overlook, packed on any warm weekend. Free, open daily.

A 1922 movie-palace landmark and the heart of the Castro, famous for its Wurlitzer organ and sing-alongs. Reopened February 2026 after a $41M restoration, now with flexible seating for films and concerts.
sights.k: Reopened February 2026 after a two-year renovation led by Another Planet Entertainment; programming now mixes film with concerts and events - check the calendar.

sights.address: 501 Twin Peaks Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94114
sights.w: The near-geographic center of the city and its best 360-degree panorama, from downtown and the bridges to the ocean. Free; open daily 5am-midnight.

The first stand-alone museum of LGBTQ history and culture in the US, in the Castro, drawing on the GLBT Historical Society's archive (Harvey Milk material included). Open Tue-Sun; free first Wednesdays.
The densest concentration of murals in the Mission - a one-block alley off 24th Street painted since the 1970s with Latin-American political and cultural art, continuously renewed. Free, always open.

sights.address: Bernal Heights Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94110
sights.w: A grassy, car-free hilltop above the Mission with a mellow local vibe and a wide-open view of downtown and the bay; a favorite dog and sunset spot. Free, open daily.
